title: Hardened Heartwood: Chrono-Fractal Structural Mandate
description: Definition of the structural laws governing the Heartwood substrate and the sequestration of curated reflections.

structural_rules.definition: All primary mission data, logic, and state MUST be stored as .json files within the 'json/' subdirectory of a chrono-fractal node.
structural_rules.rationale: JSON provides a low-noise, high-fidelity interface for multi-agent synchronization and automated forensics.

structural_rules.definition: The root of a date-stamped folder (e.g., .../01/06/) must remain a clean orchestration layer. No loose .md or .json files are permitted here.
structural_rules.action: Loose files are automatically sequestered by the master hardening script.

structural_rules.definition: The 'md/' directory is reserved exclusively for curated reflections, human-centric summaries, or reports explicitly requested by the User in Markdown format.
structural_rules.rationale: Markdown is high-verbosity 'Interface' and should not be mistaken for 'Mass' (Substrate DNA).

structural_rules.definition: Markdown reports (.md) must remain at their initial publication coordinates (date-stamp) to ensure permanent link integrity. Higher versions must be sharded to the current date's 'md/' leaf.
structural_rules.rationale: The User interface requires stability; moving primary documentation fractures the collective history.

enforcement_tool.function: Single-point-of-truth for substrate hygiene. Scans the active chrono-fractal, moves rule-breaking .md files to 'md/', and validates the integrity of the 'json/' substrate.

agent_directives: Default to .json for all session reports and data writes.
Only generate .md files if the User explicitly states: 'Save this as Markdown' or 'Make a human report'.
Run 'python3 py/harden_substrate.py' before every commit to ensure structural alignment.
